messages:
nina: FYI customers keep hitting an onboarding footgun: our Go quickstart for generator streaming shows client created with context.Background(), then people cancel request ctx and wonder why goroutines hang.

pras: That snippet is dangerously minimal. We should show request-scoped usage and an explicit defer Close(). Proposed snippet to paste into quickstart:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 25*time.Second)
defer cancel()
// client can be global; pass ctx into streaming call
gen := client.Generator(ctx, req)
defer func() { _ = gen.Close() }()
for gen.Next() { token := gen.Token(); _ = token }
```
Also call out: "Do not use context.Background() for streams created inside handlers."

omar: There's a companion bug in the retry helper: during backoff we used time.Sleep, which ignores ctx. I changed it to use time.NewTimer + select on timer.C and ctx.Done() so retries abort when the parent context is canceled.

pras: Can you add a tiny integration test that starts a generator, cancels the context, and asserts goroutine count returns to baseline within 200ms? That would catch regressions in CI.

omar: Yep, added streaming_leak_test.go with that check and a flakiness guard. Pushed branch fix/go-gen-ctx-leak.

ci-bot: CI: build 8021 on fix/go-gen-ctx-leak passed :white_check_mark:

nina: Great. Follow-ups: docs PR to update quickstart + short sidebar about request ctx vs Background(), merge retry fix, and file an RFC to standardize stream API names (Close vs CloseStream). I'll open the docs PR and link the test and retry patch.
